The process of executing a program in a computer system follows a Fetch–Decode–Execute Cycle, coordinated by various registers and the control unit.

🔸 Step-by-Step Execution Process:

  1. Program Loading:
    The program is loaded into main memory from an input device.

  2. Fetching the Instruction:

    • The Program Counter (PC) is set to the address of the first instruction.

    • The PC’s value is transferred to the Memory Address Register (MAR).

    • A Read signal is sent to memory.

    • The instruction is fetched from memory into the Memory Data Register (MDR) and then transferred to the Instruction Register (IR).

  3. Decoding the Instruction:

    • The Control Unit examines the operation field of the instruction in the IR to determine the type of operation (e.g., ADD, LOAD).

  4. Fetching Operands:

    • If the operation requires operands, the addresses are sent to MAR, and operands are fetched into MDR.

    • These are then passed to General-Purpose Registers or directly to the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU).

  5. Executing the Instruction:

    • The ALU performs the specified operation on the operands.

    • The result is sent to MDR.

    • The address of the destination (memory/register) is sent to MAR, and a Write operation stores the result.

  6. PC Increment:

    • After execution, the PC is incremented to point to the next instruction in sequence.

🔸 Role of Registers and ALU:

  • MAR: Holds the address of memory to access.

  • MDR: Temporarily holds data read from or written to memory.

  • IR: Stores the instruction currently being executed.

  • PC: Keeps track of instruction sequence.

  • General-Purpose Registers: Temporarily hold data or results.

  • ALU: Performs all arithmetic and logic operations.

🔸 Conclusion:

This cycle continues until the program completes. The coordination between memory, registers, ALU, and control unit ensures smooth and efficient execution of instructions in a computer system.
